SRINAGAR: A new poster issued by the little-known United Liberation Council (ULC) threatening Kashmiri Pandits led community members working in the Kashmir Valley under the PM Package for Kashmiri Migrants and Non-Migrant Kashmiri Pandits to write to J&K chief secretary Atal Dulloo seeking enhanced security. Chief minister Omar Abdullah described the threats as “highly concerning.”The poster contains the personal details of some Kashmiri Pandit employees, including addresses.Omar, talking to reporters here, urged police and law-and-order agencies not to take the threats lightly. He said the agencies have a responsibility to provide security to Kashmiri Pandit employees and urged them to proactively investigate the source of the threats.“In a similar situation around two and a half years ago, some Pandit employees were targeted,” Omar said. He said security and law-and-order arrangements in J&K are under the control of the lieutenant-governor.The police have issued any statement on the fresh threat. The chief secretary was not available for comment.According to a letter from All PM Package Employees’ Forum to the CS, “a fresh threat poster, purportedly issued by a terrorist outfit calling itself the United Liberation Council (ULC) on Aug 23, 2026, has surfaced on social media.The poster reportedly contains threats directed towards migrant Kashmiri Pandit employees and … details such as names, addresses and vehicle numbers of certain individuals.”While the forum said the “authenticity of the poster is yet to be verified by police and security agencies”, it added that “the repeated circulation of such threat letters and posters, particularly those containing sensitive personal information, is a matter of grave concern”.The forum sought a review of security arrangements at places of posting, residential accommodation and transit routes of PM Package employees. It said govt should ensure that employees whose names, addresses or vehicle details have appeared in such threats receive immediate protection and necessary security guidance.All Minority Employees Association president Sanjay Kaul said the Aug 23 poster was the third in 20 days. “We are only here for work. We take such threat letters seriously as they contain names and even numbers of vehicles of some Pandit employees,” Kaul said. “Before 2022 we were working fearlessly, but not now. We seek a thorough probe,” he added.In May 2022, Kashmiri Pandit migrant employee Rahul Bhat was shot dead by terrorists inside his office in central Kashmir’s Budgam district. He was recruited as a clerk under the PM Package for migrants in 2010-11.The Manmohan Singh-led UPA govt had in 2008 introduced a rehabilitation package for Kashmiri Pandits living outside the Valley, including providing 6,000 govt jobs and creation of new posts. Those recruited under the package are posted in various govt departments across Kashmir and commonly referred to as “PM package employees”.
Article Summary: A new poster issued by the little-known United Liberation Council (ULC) threatens Kashmiri Pandits. Chief minister Omar Abdullah described the threats as “highly concerning” The poster contains the personal details of some KashmiriPandit employees, including addresses.

Article Title: No alliance with SAD? BL Santosh says BJP to go solo in Punjab polls

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party on Monday put speculation over an alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal to rest, saying the saffron party will contest all 117 seats in the upcoming Punjab assembly elections.BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh said the party was fully prepared for the polls and would form the government in Punjab."Punjab is fully ready for change, and the BJP is fully prepared to make this change a reality. In the upcoming assembly elections, the BJP will contest all 117 Assembly seats in Punjab and, by securing a victory, will form its government in the state," Santosh said.The statement comes days after speculation grew over a possible BJP-SAD alliance following SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal's meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Former Union minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal had also hinted at the possibility of the Akali Dal joining hands with the BJP again, while expressing a cryptic wish for "agreements" that brought progress to Punjab from Delhi.Earlier, Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia also said that people in Punjab want his party to join hands with the Bharatiya Janata Party for the upcoming polls.Majithia cited Punjab's status as a border state and the need to protect social harmony and the state's social fabric as reasons for public sentiment favouring a reunion."We should understand that the Shiromani Akali Dal and BJP have worked together. Vajpayee ji and Badal ji strengthened this alliance, and it continued during Modi ji's time," Majithia said.The SAD had parted ways with the National Democratic Alliance in September 2020 over the three farm laws, which were later repealed.Santosh began his two-day visit to Punjab to review the party's organisational functioning and strengthen coordination and preparedness at the grassroots level in the poll-bound state.His visit comes amid dissent within the BJP's state unit over a recent organisational reshuffle, with a section of leaders accusing the state leadership of sidelining the old cadre.
Article Summary: BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh said the party was fully prepared for the polls and would form the government in Punjab. Article Title: Govt seeks generation data from rooftop solar
Article Text:
Rooftop solar (RTS) systems under the PM Surya Ghar scheme. Photo credit : PTI

NEW DELHI: As the number of households installing rooftop solar (RTS) systems under the PM Surya Ghar scheme rises and renewable energy capacity increases, govt has decided to track how much electricity these systems are actually generating, with inverter makers required to share daily generation data with the national portal.The move could give govt, for the first time, a system to monitor the performance of individual RTS installations rather than merely track the capacity added under the scheme.Under new guidelines issued by the ministry of new and renewable energy, inverter manufacturers will have to provide daily cumulative generation data through an API to the national portal, mapped to the device’s serial number. The guidelines also require applications, monitoring and control servers and cloud-hosted data linked to inverter systems to be located in India.The data could help govt assess how much electricity rooftop systems are actually generating and identify under-performing installations. It could also allow generation to be analysed across states and power distribution companies (discoms), providing a clearer picture of the energy benefits being delivered by the scheme.A govt-appointed Expert Committee on Energy Statistics also flagged the absence of comprehensive data on electricity generated and consumed by decentralised renewable energy systems in a recent report.Currently, more than 44 lakh RTS systems have been installed under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSGMBY), benefiting over 52 lakh households and adding 15.6 GW of solar capacity.The committee noted that electricity generated by rooftop solar systems is often consumed at the premises and does not pass through the grid, leaving it outside conventional electricity supply statistics. It said generation, export and self-consumption data from rooftop systems are not uniformly recorded or aggregated by discoms and recommended mandatory collection and reporting of such data to improve the accuracy of India’s electricity statistics.“Electricity generated from many of these systems is already metered. However, these meter readings are either not visible to the discoms or, even if they are visible, the readings are not recorded systematically and reported,” the committee said.Alekhya Datta, director, electricity and renewables division, TERI, said national-level centralised monitoring of electricity generation from rooftop solar systems would have multiple benefits. “If electricity distribution companies have data on electricity generated by rooftop solar plants (behind the meter) in their respective areas and the units consumed by consumers, they will be able to plan their power purchases accordingly,” Datta said.“The amount of electricity generated by RTS plants will also give an indication of the quality of the system, and this attribute can be used in a vendor rating system as well as help improve operations and maintenance. Consumers, too, will get a sense of satisfaction from knowing their contribution to the environment.”Though the ministry has asked all inverter companies to share daily generation data, Datta said only around 15 per cent of inverters currently have the capability to share it through APIs. The govt is also yet to create an integrated dashboard where the data can be collated.
Article Summary: The move could give govt, for the first time, a system to monitor the performance of individual RTS installations. More than 44 lakh RTS systems have been installed under the PM Surya Ghar scheme. Data could help govt assess how much electricity rooftop systems are actually generating.

Article Title: 'Hindu baiter': CM Himanta slams Rahul Gandhi over Manusmriti row
Article Text:
Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma slams Rahul Gandhi over Manusmriti comment. Photo credit: ANI

NEW DELHI: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Monday joined the escalating political row over Rahul Gandhi ’s remarks on the Manusmriti, accusing the Congress leader of using women’s rights as a 'smokescreen' to target Hinduism and challenging him to support a Uniform Civil Code (UCC).Sarma, in a post on X, said, “Rahul Gandhi is NO champion of women’s rights. He is simply a Hindu baiter, using the cause of women’s empowerment as a convenient smokescreen to target and discredit Hindu Dharma.”The Assam chief minister’s remarks came after Gandhi, during an interaction with girl students in Pune on Saturday, criticised what he called a “Manusmriti mindset” and urged women to “smash patriarchy”.Sarma questioned Gandhi’s position by asking, “Consider this: how many times has he spoken with the same outrage against patriarchal and medieval practices that persist under Sharia? NEVER.”He further argued that Manusmriti and Sharia should not be treated as equivalent sources of authority, writing, “While Sharia is foundational to Islamic jurisprudence, Manusmriti has no comparable scriptural authority in Hindu Dharma. It is not even a universally binding code for Hindus.”Sarma then directly challenged the Congress leader over the issue of a common civil law. “So here is a simple challenge to Rahul Gandhi: If women’s equality truly comes before politics, will he unequivocally support a Uniform Civil Code that guarantees equal rights irrespective of religion?” he said.Sarma also alleged that Congress had a record of compromising on women’s rights, referring to the Shah Bano case and the Triple Talaq legislation. He further claimed that Gandhi had ensured that no woman was included in the Karnataka state Cabinet.The remarks came after the LoP’s interaction with students, where he said women should not be defined solely through their relationships with men.Rahul said women belong to themselves and not to their fathers, husbands or sons, while describing as shameful the Manusmriti’s prescription that women remain under the authority of male relatives at different stages of their lives.Referring to a verse from the ancient text, Gandhi said, “These words are a shame. These words should not have been spoken.”The controversy has since widened, with Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath, Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis among other prominent BJP faces criticised Rahul’s remarks.CM Adityanath earlier questioned Gandhi’s role as Leader of Opposition and said, “Whether you accept the Manusmriti or not is your choice, but do not acquaint people with wrong facts.”
Article Summary: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma slams Rahul Gandhi over Manusmriti comment. Accuses Congress leader of using women’s rights as a'smokescreen' to target Hinduism. Sarma also challenges Gandhi to support a Uniform Civil Code.

Article Title: Kejriwal to address town hall on E20 petrol policy during Goa visit

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Arvind Kejriwal will address a town hall on E20 petrol policy during his two-day visit to Goa beginning Monday.Kejriwal landed at Dabolim Airport in south Goa on Sunday, where he was received by local party leaders.AAP sources said Kejriwal would address a press conference on Monday in Panaji and a town hall a day later on E20 petrol policy.The AAP, which has two MLAs in the 40-member Goa assembly, has announced a campaign against the "forced implementation" of E20 (ethanol-blended) fuel in the coastal state, which will go to polls in 2027.Earlier this month, Kejriwal had demanded the government give the option to choose between pure petrol and E20 at fuel pumps.The Centre introduced E20, a blend of 20 per cent ethanol and 80 per cent petrol, as part of efforts to reduce vehicular emissions and cut dependence on crude oil imports. After a phased rollout, E20 became the only petrol variant available at fuel pumps across the country from April 2026.The move has triggered concerns among some vehicle owners, with motorists reporting reduced engine performance and apprehensions about damage to fuel lines and other components.Owners of older vehicles, many of which may not have been designed for high ethanol blends, have been seeking availability of lower blends such as E10.Industry executives had sought to allay concerns over the use of E20 petrol, saying the fuel has undergone rigorous scientific testing, is safe for both new and older vehicles, and is critical for reducing India's dependence on imported crude oil.
Article Summary: Kejriwal landed at Dabolim Airport in south Goa on Sunday, where he was received by local party leaders. AAP has announced a campaign against the "forced implementation" of E20 (ethanol-blended) fuel in the coastal state, which will go to polls in 2027.

Article Title: TMC moves SC against delay in disqualification of 20 rebel MPs
Article Text:
Abhishek Banerjee seeks SC direction on disqualification of 20 TMC MPs. Photo credit: PTI

NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress (TMC) general secretary and Lok Sabha MP Abhishek Banerjee has moved Supreme Court seeking an early decision by Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla on disqualification pleas against 20 rebel party MPs. The matter is scheduled to come up for hearing before the apex court on Tuesday.Banerjee has challenged the alleged delay in deciding the disqualification petitions, which were filed against MPs accused by the TMC of abandoning the party and aligning themselves with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI).According to Supreme Court website, a bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana will hear Banerjee’s plea on August 25.Banerjee has urged the apex court to direct speaker Om Birla to expeditiously decide the pending disqualification proceedings.The TMC has maintained that the 20 MPs were elected on the party’s symbol and that their subsequent alignment with another political formation amounts to voluntarily giving up membership of the party. The party has argued that such conduct attracts disqualification under the anti-defection provisions of the Constitution.The rebel MPs, however, have maintained that their move constitutes a valid merger.The petition names the Lok Sabha speaker and the house secretary general as respondents, besides the 20 MPs against whom the disqualification proceedings have been sought.The MPs named in the petition are Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, Sudip Bandyopadhyay, Satabdi Roy, Prasun Banerjee, Rachana Banerjee, Jagadish Chandra Barma Basunia, Partha Bhowmick, Arup Chakraborty, Adhikari Deepak Dev, Sayani Ghosh, Bapi Haldar, Md Abu Taher Khan, Kalipada Saren Kherwal, Asit Kumar Mal, June Maliah, Mitali Bag, Khalilur Rahaman, Mala Roy, Sharmila Sarkar and Yusuf Pathan.The TMC has alleged that the rebel MPs have subsequently been treated as an NCPI group in Parliament and have participated in National Democratic Alliance (NDA) parliamentary activities.The case comes against the backdrop of a broader political realignment in West Bengal following the TMC’s defeat in the 2026 Assembly elections.Supreme Court is also hearing a separate petition by Shiv Sena (UBT) challenging the Speaker’s approval of the merger of six of its MPs with the Shiv Sena led by Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde. That matter is being heard by a bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe.
Article Summary: Abhishek Banerjee seeks an early decision by Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla on disqualification pleas against 20 rebel party MPs. The matter is scheduled to come up for hearing before the apex court on Tuesday. The TMC has alleged that the rebel MPs have subsequently been treated as an NCPI group in Parliament.
